————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, the November 18, 2002/Kartika 27, 1924 (Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Development of North Eastern Region; Disinvestment; Health and
Family Welfare; Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Information and
Broadcasting; Law and Justice; Shipping; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Urban Development and Poverty Alleviation)
Total number of questions—20
1
Functioning of the CGHS dispensaries
*1. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
complaints from the beneficiaries of the
Central Government Health Scheme that
attendance of doctors and para-medical
staff is not satisfactory in dispensaries and
medicines are generally not available and
also medical equipments like X-ray
machines are not in working condition; and
(b) the steps taken or proposed to be
taken to improve the conditions in CGHS
dispensaries and hospitals?
Mala-fide propaganda by Pakistan
†*2.  SHRI BALKAVI BAIRAGI: Will
the Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are proposing
to ban PTV apart from other measures to
counter the mala-fide propaganda by
Pakistan;
(b) whether a special group comprising
high officials, constituted for the purpose
by Government has submitted its report
to Government; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Increase in heart diseases
*3. SHRI H.K. JAVARE GOWDA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the heart
disease scenario in the country is alarming
and geting worse every year;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
treatment of heart disease is so costly that
the common man is not in a position to meet
the expenses and is left to die;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor;
(e) whether Government propose to
give free medical treatment for heart
disease; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Alzheimer disease
*4. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether WHO has reported that

Alzheimer disease;
(b) whether this disease is more sinister
than AIDS and cancer; and

Sale of spurious drugs in Delhi
*5. SHRI GAYA SINGH:
SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that recently
the sale of spurious drugs flourished in
Delhi on a large scale;
(b) if so, the details of the raids
conducted and spurious drugs confiscated;
and
(c) the measures taken to check such a
heinous crime?
Functioning of DD Kendra, Silchar,
Assam
*6. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of
INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the near-stalemate condition of the
functioning of Doordarshan Kendra,
Silchar, Assam;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken in
this regard to tone up the working of the
DD Kendra, Silchar?
Community TV/Radio transmission
projects for universities
†*7. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have
introduced a project to permit some
universities and institutions limited
community TV/Radio transmission
through narrowcast technology;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the cities in the country, particularly
in Andhra Pradesh, where it is proposed to
be introduced?
Coverage of AIR and DD
*8. SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT
RAO:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
 Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to cover all far-flung areas under the KU
Band-higher band frequency to widen the
coverage of Doordarshan and All India
Radio;
(b) whether there are still large areas
of the States not covered by Doordarshan
and All India Radio;
(c) if so, the steps being considered in
this regard; and
(d) by when proposals in this regard
are likely to be implemented?

Total number of questions—141
1
Development of NER
1. SHRI RAJU PARMAR:
SHRI BHAGATRAM
MANHAR:
 Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT
OF NORTH EASTERN REGION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned
“Development of North-East a priority,
says Shourie” which appeared in the Times
of India, New Delhi, dated 4th October,
2002;
(b) whether the North Eastern Region
would soon become the hub of international
investment from being a hot bed of
insurgency;
(c) if so, whether Government are aware
that payments to industrial houses, SSI units
and others are not being made by North
Eastern States, particularly Government of
Manipur; and
(d) if so, to what extent the development
of North East would be viable when the
payments for projects are not cleared
promptly by these States?
Utilisation of funds for the
development of NER
2. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of
DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH
EASTERN REGION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that no expenditure
has been incurred during the last two years
out of the funds allocated for the development
of the entire North Eastern Region;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps taken/proposed to be
taken to draw up quick developmental
programmes for the proper utilisation of
the funds earmarked for the purpose?
Delay on disinvestment
3. SHRI MOOLCHAND MEENA:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the delay in disinvestment
has proved bad for market and
Government’s image;
(b) if so, whether the Indian industry is
not happy about the recent flip-flop on
disinvestment;

2
WIN2\SESSION\3667RS.PM5
(c) whether according to them the
disinvestment fiasco would adversely affect
the market sentiment and the overall
economic sentiments;
(d) if so, whether both the Prime
Minister and the Deputy Prime Minister
have been urged to take immediate final
decision for continuance of disinvestment
policy; and
(e) if so, by when Government are likely
to take final decision on these issues?
Evaluation of industries for
disinvestment
†4. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
‘LALAN’:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of
DISINVESTMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether evaluation of PSUs is done
after selection of industries for
disinvestment by Government;
(b) if so, names of the PSUs that have
been selected for evaluation by
Government, so far; and
(c) the amount paid to the evaluating
institutions?
Heavy industries for disinvestment
†5. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
 Will the Minister of DISINVEST-
MENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have identified
heavy industries which have been selected
for disinvestment;
(b) if so, the names of the industries for
which decision has been taken to make
disinvestment and when; and
(c) the basis of the priority fixed for
disinvestment?
Time-bound programme for
disinvestment of heavy industries
†6. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that any time-
bound programme for disinvestment of
industries under Ministry of Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises has been
fixed;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have laid down
any criteria for priority disinvestment; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Strategic sale of BPCL and HPCL
7. SHRI N.R. DASARI:
SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been resistance
from the opposition as well as from some
quarters in the ruling alliance including the
Union Ministers against Government’s
proposal for the strategic sale of BPCL and
HPCL; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
present stage of the proposal?
Sale of Hotel Centaur
8. SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of
DISINVESTMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned,

Sahara Group is illegal; and
(c) whether Government are now
